title: DC-area forecast: A few showers or a storm before midnight; trending cool and wet into midweek
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Late afternoon and evening 70s have some mugginess still. A few showers and a rumble of thunder are possible this evening through around midnight.

What's next? Trending cooler Monday as showers could turn more numerous at some point in the afternoon. Low pressure keeps rain likely Monday night into Tuesday and Wednesday, with a gusty breeze and cool highs mainly in the 60s.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Scattered showers and a storm remain possible this evening before diminishing overnight. It's rather muggy until humidity drops a bit toward morning. Lows within a few degrees of 65. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow (Monday): Mostly cloudy to start the work week. Only a stray shower possibly through around noon. Scattered and a storm could develop at some point during the afternoon. A cool breeze from the north and northeast helps limit highs to the upper 60s (cloudiest spots) to mid-70s (sunniest spots). Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Showers, and possibly a storm, are likely at times during the evening and overnight, with some pockets of soaking rain possible. Remaining mostly cloudy with lows near 60. Confidence: Medium

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

This disturbed pattern continues with rain likely at times Tuesday into Wednesday. Both days could see a gusty wind from the northeast with highs well below average, probably only in the 60s. You might need to break out the long sleeves or light jacket for the first time in a while! Tuesday and Wednesday night lows drop back to the 60s. Confidence: Low-Medium

Thursday looks less wet, but clouds and a chance of showers may persist with highs held to the 60s again. Skies should brighten by Friday, when rain chances look lower with highs back up to near 70. Confidence: Low

Today’s daily digit — 5/10: Mostly gray skies, kind of sticky, and some pesky shower potential. Blah. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale

DC weather history for September 20

Rain from the approach of the 1938 hurricane set a daily record locally, a prelude to the catastrophic impacts the storm would unleash farther north in New England.
